title: Eagles - Hotel California (guitar solo section) - NOT USABLE for the seventh gate, see notes
source: Real bs_roformer_sw stems (bass/drums/guitar) of the solo section, 62.6s. Chart is the Ultimate Guitar official chart, which is written in a DIFFERENT KEY from this audio.
key_note: The CHART is in Bm. This AUDIO is in Dm - a minor third (+3 semitones) above it. Verified: 5 of 5 detected roots are explained by the chart transposed +3, and 0 of 5 at +2 or +4. The pipeline independently called the key D minor at 0.913 confidence, which is correct for this audio.
chords_note: The chart's Bm F# A E / G D Em F#7 transposed +3 to match the audio.
notes: DO NOT use this excerpt to calibrate CHORD_SEVENTH_ABSENCE_RATIO. It cannot answer the question, and here is the measurement that shows why: the guitar stem averages 1.76 chroma bins above half the frame peak. A triad reads about 3, a two-note harmonised lead about 2, a single line about 1. This section's guitar stem is the harmonised twin lead, NOT the rhythm chords - so there is no third present to detect, and 100% of beats read as power chords against a chart with none.

The missing chord is exactly the one needed: the V (F# in Bm, A in Dm) is the only chart root the pipeline never found. Its pitch class is actually well represented in both stems (guitar 10.5%, bass 12.9%), so it is not absent from the audio - the two-note lead texture just never states it as a chord.
Root layer did well given lead-only input: 5 of 6 chart roots found, ZERO spurious roots.

Beat grid ruled out as the cause: forcing grids at 74, 99 and 148 bpm plus half-time all gave the same 5 roots, the same missing A, and the same 100% power chords. Detected tempo is 99.4bpm regardless of the start_bpm prior, against the chart's 74 - consistent with this being a different arrangement, not a tracking error.

TO ACTUALLY CALIBRATE THE SEVENTH GATE, two things are needed: (a) the 'other' (and piano) stem as well as guitar - the acoustic/12-string rhythm part is probably in there, since it is not in the guitar stem; and (b) ideally a VERSE or CHORUS section rather than the solo, where the rhythm guitar carries the harmony and no lead is playing over it. The verse progression is identical to the solo's, so it tests the same chords.
Also note for scoring: if a chart and an audio version disagree on key, transpose the chart, do not transpose the detection. The app reports sounding pitch.
